Key Factors When Comparing Roman and Cellular Shades

Honeycomb shades are designed with air pockets that trap air, creating an insulating barrier to help buffer heat transfer at the glass., whereas fabric Roman treatments prioritize tailored drapery folds over air-trapping pockets. Homeowners researching cellular vs roman window coverings often ask whether Roman shades are out of style in 2026, what the practical downsides of each style are, and how the newest window covering trends compare for daily light management. Selecting between these two categories comes down to thermal performance at the glass, stack height when raised, and available frame depth.

When we evaluate windows at In the Shade, we check window frame squareness, bracket depth, and cord safety before quoting an inside or outside mount. Evaluating a Roman Shade VS Cellular Shade requires balancing how much top glass a raised fabric stack covers against how tightly an accordion pleat compresses into the headrail. For nurseries and pet-friendly rooms, we recommend cordless or motorized Hunter Douglas operating systems to eliminate dangling lift cords and keep operation smooth.

  • Thermal Insulation Performance: Cellular pockets trap air between the room and the window pane to help buffer temperature swings, while Roman shades rely on optional thermal or blackout linings.
  • Raised Stack Height: Honeycomb pleats compress tightly against the top casing, whereas cascading Roman folds hang down several inches and may partially cover upper glass.
  • Light Control Flexibility: Operating options such as Top-Down Bottom-Up hardware allow cellular and select woven shades to lower from the top for daylight while maintaining lower-window privacy.
  • Maintenance and Dusting: Smooth or pleated honeycomb cells vacuum quickly with a brush attachment, while deep fabric folds on Roman shades require regular dusting to prevent buildup.

Tailored Fabric Folds Versus Honeycomb Air Cells

Roman shades construct visible design statements using continuous textiles that gather into soft horizontal pleats or flat panels when raised. Adding Blackout roman shades lining helps block streetlamps and early morning sun in sleeping areas, though light can still halo around the edges of an inside-mount fabric panel. Homeowners who want pattern variety, natural woven textures, or drapery-weight fabrics choose Roman styles to coordinate with room upholstery.

Cellular shades use engineered honeycomb pockets that expand to filter glare or block light while maintaining a slim, architectural profile. Because the lift cords run inside the air cells on standard cordless models, there are no visible rout holes leaking pinpricks of sunlight into the room. If your priority is keeping the view completely unobstructed when the treatment is fully raised, choose a compact cellular shade over a bulky fabric fold.

Mounting Depth Requirements For Older Frames

Narrow historic windows measuring 24 to 36 inches wide require a minimum of 1 inch of flat mounting depth for secure inside mounts, and shallow window recesses favor compact honeycomb profiles. Older replacement frames or shallow plaster casings frequently leave too little interior clearance for deep Roman shade headrails, forcing an outside mount above the trim. Compact cellular headrails sit flush inside tighter jambs without protruding into the room.

Because older window frames settle over time and are rarely perfectly square, we measure width and height at three separate points, top, middle, and bottom, to prevent fabric edges from rubbing against the jamb. When we inspect a window with less than 1 inch of flat mounting clearance due to protruding sash locks or cranks, we specify an outside-mounted Roman shade or a low-profile cellular bracket so hardware operates cleanly.

Evaluating the price comparison and advantages between soft fabric folds and cellular shades comes down to whether your budget prioritizes artisanal textiles or air-trapping pockets. When homeowners here compare types of window coverings for multi-panel bay windows spanning 6 to 10 feet, we recommend cellular styles when budget and compact headrail clearance matter most, as hand-sewn drapery panels require higher fabric yardage and deeper brackets across each angled section.
